newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds were propelled to a sharply higher close by strength in German bund futures but selling remained the favoured strategy of market players.
This pressure hampered the rise in Dutch state loans, which underperformed their German equivalents, and was more marked in shorter to middle maturities, dealers said.
"There seems to be a distinct lack of buyers around now," said one dealer.
He said the recent issuance of a new 10-year benchmark, the 5.75 percent February 2007 bond, combined with continued Eurobond issuance in guilders, were contributing to the tone.
"We haven't really absorbed the new bond yet," he said.
Another dealer reported selling pressure on the new 10-year and the April 2010 bonds but said March and November 2005 paper was better bid.
He said although the Dutch market lagged the rise of Germany, he detected an improved undertone as the day wore on.
"I have a suspicion the worst is over," the dealer said.
The new 10-year bellweather closed at a bid yield of 5.60 percent, the lowest finish since the Finance Ministry first issued them two weeks ago, versus 5.66 percent on Tuesday.
Contributing to the strength in bunds, which prompted dealers to mark up Dutch bonds, was weaker than expected December industrial orders in Germany.
Early in the day, Dutch local authorities borrower BNG issued 1.0 billion guilders of bonds with a coupon and maturity matching the new benchmark.
Dealers said the market was looking for direction and awaiting the outcome of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee's deliberations on U.S. interest rates, expected after the Dutch market closes.
